content.title: About
content.content: The chicken, bean and cheese burrito is a Mexican‑inspired dish consisting of a large soft flour tortilla filled with sautéed chicken pieces, cooked beans, melted cheese, and often rice, salsa and sour cream. It combines protein, fiber and bold flavors in a convenient handheld meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos as we know them today originated in the northern United States, where Mexican cuisine merged with local ingredients.
Traditional Mexican burritos were simple, usually just beans and rice; chicken and cheese became popular in the U.S. in the 20th century.
Flour tortillas are preferred for burritos because they are more pliable than corn tortillas.
Burritos are commonly served with guacamole, adding heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats.
The United States celebrates National Burrito Day on the first Thursday of March.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides a complete source of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Fiber from beans
items.content: Beans supply soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, nutrients important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and beans are rich in B‑vitamins such as B6 and folate, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate saturated fat
items.content: When made with lean chicken breast and low‑fat cheese, the burrito can be relatively low in saturated fat.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese can be high in salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Large burritos can be calorie‑dense due to the tortilla and cheese, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Chicken safety
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F) to prevent salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are eaten by hand, often sliced in half. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or fresh veggies. For a lighter option, choose a whole‑grain tortilla and reduced‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared burrito in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Freeze in a separate bag at –18 °C; reheat in the microwave or oven before serving.
